name: Nabal
overview: Nabal was a male member of the tribe of Judah known as the rich man of Maon and the husband of Abigail. His description in Scripture highlights his wealth and geographical association. There are no additional notes provided about his character or actions beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Nabal means "fool" in Hebrew, which is a proper name but not one given by God. This meaning may reflect aspects of his character as implied by the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Nabal is identified as a descendant of Caleb and is married to Abigail. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Nabal's significance in the biblical account centers on his identity as a wealthy man in Maon and his marriage to Abigail. His name meaning "fool" suggests a negative portrayal, which is consistent with the narrative context in 1 Samuel 25:3. As a descendant of Caleb, he is connected to a notable lineage within the tribe of Judah.
